question_tree.question: When you plug in the charger, does the charging light on the laptop turn on?

next.text:
1. Check the charger's cable and plug firmly at both ends, and try a different wall socket.
2. If you have a spare charger of the same type, try it. Chargers fail more often than laptops do.
3. Look inside the charging port for dust or bent pins, and gently clean it with a dry toothpick or air blower. Don't use metal tools.
4. If a known-good charger still doesn't light it up, the charging port may need repair.

options.answer: Yes, the light is on but the battery isn't charging

next.text:
1. Restart the laptop. Then open Device Manager, expand 'Batteries', right-click 'Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery', uninstall it, and restart the laptop.
2. Check the laptop maker's website for a battery or BIOS update.
3. If the battery is more than 3 years old and has been heavily used, it may be worn out and need replacing.

question_tree.question: When you press the power button, do any lights come on or does the fan spin?

next.text:
1. Plug in the charger and leave it for 30 minutes, since a fully drained battery can take a while to show signs of life.
2. Unplug the charger, hold the power button for 30 seconds to drain leftover power, then plug the charger in and try again.
3. Try a different wall socket and, if you have one, a different compatible charger.
4. If it's still dead, a technician should check the charging circuit or battery.

options.answer: Lights or fans come on but the screen stays black

next.text:
1. Shine a torch at the screen and look closely. If you can faintly see the picture, the screen's backlight has failed.
2. Plug in an external monitor. If it works there, the laptop is fine and the screen or its cable needs repair.
3. Restart after holding the power button for 30 seconds, and try with the charger unplugged and plugged in.
4. If neither screen shows a picture, see the 'No display / black screen on boot' guide.

title: Laptop overheating or fan too loud

question_tree.question: Is your laptop sitting on a soft surface like a bed, sofa or your lap?

next.text:
1. Soft surfaces block the air vents underneath and quickly cause overheating. Use a hard flat surface like a desk.
2. A laptop cooling stand that lifts the laptop and adds fans can help a lot.
3. Check the vents on the sides and back and make sure nothing is blocking them.

options.answer: No, it's on a hard surface and it's still hot and loud

next.text:
1. Dust inside the laptop is the most common cause. Blow compressed air into the side and back vents in short bursts.
2. Check the programs using the processor in Task Manager and close the ones you don't need.
3. If your laptop is more than 2 to 3 years old, the cooling fan or thermal paste may need cleaning or replacing — a repair shop can do this.
4. In Windows power settings, choose 'Balanced' mode rather than 'Best performance' when you don't need the extra speed.

title: Laptop screen is black but the laptop is on

question_tree.question: If you connect the laptop to an external monitor or TV, does the picture show up there?

next.text:
1. Your laptop itself is working, so the problem is the laptop's screen, or the cable that connects the screen to the laptop.
2. Check whether the laptop is still under warranty, because screen repairs can be expensive.
3. A repair shop can test the screen cable and the backlight to find out which part has failed.

options.answer: No, the external screen shows nothing either

next.text:
1. Hold the power button for 30 seconds with the charger and battery (if removable) disconnected, then reconnect and try again.
2. If your laptop has removable RAM, switch off, take out the RAM, and press it firmly back in.
3. If it still shows nothing anywhere, see the 'No display / black screen on boot' guide, or take it to a technician.

title: Some laptop keyboard keys not working

question_tree.question: Are only a few keys not working, or is the whole keyboard not responding?

next.text:
1. Turn the laptop off, tilt it upside down and gently tap the back to loosen dust or crumbs under the keys.
2. Blow compressed air around and under the keys in short bursts. Never pour liquid on a keyboard.
3. Use a plug-in USB keyboard for now. If a few keys are completely dead after cleaning, the keyboard can be replaced inexpensively on many laptops.

1. Restart the laptop. Then open Device Manager, find 'Keyboards', right-click 'Standard PS/2 Keyboard', and choose 'Uninstall device', then restart.
2. Check that no keys are physically stuck, and that Filter Keys or Sticky Keys isn't switched on in Accessibility settings.
3. If a plug-in USB keyboard works but the laptop keyboard doesn't, the laptop's keyboard or its internal cable needs repair.
